children: Malaysia's palm oil inventories are expected to ease in October, supported by an anticipated recovery in exports and stronger domestic consumption ahead of Diwali, Public Investment Bank analyst Chong Hoe Leong says in a note. September stocks rose as production hit a record 2.1 million tons while exports fell to a seven-month low of 1.1 million tons amid stiff competition from Indonesia. However, severe forest fires and haze in Indonesia could disrupt harvesting and reduce output in coming months, he adds. Public IB maintains an overweight rating on Malaysian plantations, pegging Sarawak Plantation and TA Ann as top picks. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
